anomalies.observed: On the LEDs sheet, Q7 is a MOSFET whose pin 2 is tied directly to the 5V_switched rail (the same horizontal net that feeds U37 VCCB and every WS2812B VDD pin) and whose pin 3 is tied directly to GND, with the gate (pin 1) driven by NET0127 (the LED-enable net that also drives U37 OE and the wire-AND of the open-drain buffers on the LED Enable / E-Stop Config sheet). Q7 is therefore connected in parallel across the supply rail, not in series with it.
anomalies.expected: A power/enable MOSFET for the addressable-LED strip must sit in series between the source rail and the WS2812B VDD node (high-side or low-side switch), so that the strip supply is switched rather than shunted; the VDD rail must not be hard-tied to the same node that the switch drains to ground.

evidence.quote: LEDs sheet: top green line labelled '5V_switched' (from U37 pin 6 VCCB via C24) runs into all WS2812B VDD pins and also taps Q7 pin 2; Q7 pin 3 goes to a GND symbol; Q7 pin 1 = NET0127, which is also U37 pin 5 (OE) and the pulled-up wire-AND of U15/U25/U14 outputs.

anomalies.impact: Whenever NET0127 drives Q7 into conduction, the 5V_switched rail is shorted to GND, collapsing the rail, blowing the 16 A resettable fuse / over-current protecting 5V, and disabling the WS2812B strip and every other 5V_switched load; the LED strip is never actually gated by the enable signal as intended.

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the specification (CAN crystals are 16 MHz, the ideal-diode/LTC4412, e-stop buffers and analog switches are present), but Q7 on the LEDs sheet is wired straight across the 5V_switched rail to ground instead of in series as a load switch, which shorts the supply when the LED-enable net turns it on.
